sections.title: Introduction
sections.extract: The program of Fock--Goncharov, starting with \cite{fockgoncharov2006}, aims to describe representation spaces of hyperbolic surfaces into Lie groups by moduli spaces defined by polynomial equations. sections.title: Classical Teichmüller space
sections.extract: We start by describing the Fock--Goncharov program for the case of Lie groups of type $A_1$. sections.extract: \label{sec:ingredients} Here we review some key components of our construction. These include generalized minors (see \cref{sec:generalized-minors}), quivers (see \cref{sec:quivers}), and cluster ensembles (see \cref{sec:cluster-ensembles}).

sections.title: Coxeter elements
sections.extract: \begin{definition} For a root system generated by simple roots $\roots = \gen{\set{\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \dotsc, \alpha_r}}$, any element $c = s_{\alpha_1} s_{\alpha_2} \dotsb s_{\alpha_r}$ is a \defined{Coxeter element}. The ordering of the roots is irrelevant: any such product of all simple roots is a Coxeter element. All Coxeter elements have the same order, which is the \defined{Coxeter number}, denoted $h$.

sections.title: Ordering mutations
sections.extract: The ends of both $\murot$ and $\muflip$ are sequences of $\murowperm$ and $\mucolperm$. We must show that these permute Dynkin sub-quivers of $Q$ by switching certain vertices without changing the cluster seed, as in \cref{rem:sigma_G-action-on-Dynkin-diagram}. These are used in \cref{lem:fgcs-exists-rot-works-trivial,lem:fgcs-exists-rot-works-nontrivial,lem:fgcs-exists-flip-works} to justify the $\muint{Oi}$ parts.
